**1 — Scene:** Pizza pieces with a creamy pasta-and-lettuce salad.

**2 — Vessel:** A large, roughly square dinner plate, partly cropped. Using an estimated equivalent diameter of **27 cm**, its area is approximately **572 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Cheese-and-tomato pizza with some vegetable topping; cooked pasta with mixed vegetables; lettuce; creamy dressing. The pizza’s cheese and sauce are included in its energy density.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density → weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pizza pieces | 25% | 143 cm² × 1.3 cm = 186 ml | 0.9 → 167 g | 260 | 434 kcal |
| Pasta and mixed vegetables | 16% | 92 cm² × 2 cm = 184 ml | 0.65 → 120 g | 135 | 162 kcal |
| Lettuce | 5% | 29 cm² × 2 cm = 58 ml | 0.15 → 9 g | 15 | 1 kcal |
| Creamy dressing | 3% | 17 cm² × 0.8 cm = 14 ml | 1.0 → 14 g | 350 | 49 kcal |

The allocated areas total **49% of the plate**, consistent with the substantial empty space. Dressing is treated separately from the salad ingredients rather than counted twice.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **310 g and 650 kcal** is plausible for the visible pizza pieces and modest salad mound. Cropping, overlap and the dressing recipe introduce considerable uncertainty.
